justification: Critical: production change to 1,336 served Ashfield DCP rules (923 retired, 408 restored under the council with traced chapters, 5 retired) via migrations 100 and 101, both applied.

pre_impl.existing_data: DQ-141 read 1,336: served rules from an older council-less load of Ashfield DCP 2016, matched to Ashfield properties by document name alongside the current load.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The tracker assumed the copy only duplicated or lagged the current load; 413 rows hold text in the current PDF that the current load is missing, so retiring them all would have dropped live rules.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Retirement keeps rows (is_current FALSE); restoration sets source_council and source_chapter_key to a registered chapter with a council URL, the shape OC-12 traces.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Each row was compared with the council's current registered chapter PDFs downloaded 2026-10-10; chapter assignment requires >= 50% of the row's 8-word runs in that PDF.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend change; property pages read the same provision rows, now without the duplicates.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Without this, Ashfield properties see 894 rules twice and 29 outdated ones; with a blind retire they would lose 408 current rules.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A council-less Ashfield row is still served (DQ-141 above 0), or a restored row is untraced (OC-12 fails).
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Observed 2026-10-10: the first duplicate test (whole-row containment) called 492 rows missing from the current load; the 8-word-run test found 100 of them split differently, leaving 290 genuinely missing. DQ-141 1,336 -> 5 after 100, 5 -> 0 after 101; outreach stays 17 of 17.

functions.name: councilToDocPattern
functions.input: a former-council slug passed by the property page, such as ashfield
functions.output: a document-name pattern; every current row whose document_id matches is served, which is why both Ashfield copies were shown
functions.if_none: Unchanged by this PR: retired rows drop out because the query requires is_current.

values.value: 408 Ashfield DCP rules restored with their chapter
values.source: Ashfield DCP 2016 current registered chapter PDFs
values.if_missing: Retired rows are no longer served; restored rows keep their text, now traced.

queries.where_clause: source_council IS NULL AND is_current AND id IN (listed ids)
source_council IS NULL AND is_current AND id IN (listed ids)

break_it.scenario: A row that only this copy holds is retired by mistake and lost from the site
break_it.what_happens: Prevented: only rows whose text is in the current load, or absent from the current PDF, are retired
break_it.how: 8-word-run comparison against the current load and the current PDF

break_it.scenario: A restored row is labelled with a chapter that does not contain it
break_it.what_happens: Prevented: the chapter must hold at least half the row's 8-word runs and beat the next chapter clearly
break_it.how: per-row best-chapter score against all registered PDFs

break_it.scenario: Restored rows become untraced in the published-document claim (OC-12)
break_it.what_happens: Prevented: every assigned chapter is registered with a council URL; OC-12 still passes

break_it.scenario: Restored rows widen the undecided-scope count for Ashfield (DQ-114)
break_it.what_happens: Prevented: all restored rows already carry config_all for both scope keys

break_it.scenario: A worked example from the DCP is served on its own as if it were a rule
break_it.what_happens: Prevented for the five found here: retired by migration 101 with their text kept
break_it.how: manual read of the residual rows

post_merge.manual_verify: Migrations 100 and 101 are already applied: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-141 reads 0.
